drivers.quarry: quarry/driver (built dist). Like-for-like decoding (int8/numeric as string, timestamptz as Date, as pg does: `codecs: [codecs.int8AsString, codecs.timestamptz]`). Defaults: prepared statements (LRU 100), binary results for hot types, pipelining onto shared connections when the pool is busy (50 per connection).
drivers.quarry-candidate: quarry (like-for-like decoding) from the build at `QUARRY_DIST_CANDIDATE`, for A/B runs of a driver change against `quarry`. Only in the matrix when that variable is set.
drivers.quarry-db: quarry's query builder (`database()` from the built `dist/index.js`) on its default driver pool, for the `db.batch` scenarios only.
drivers.quarry-lossless: quarry/driver with its standalone lossless defaults: int8 as bigint, timestamptz/date as text (no Date construction).
drivers.quarry-noprep: quarry/driver with `prepare: false` (unnamed statements; text results).
drivers.quarry-nopipe: quarry/driver with `pipeline: false` (exclusive connection checkout, like pg).
drivers.pg: node-postgres 8.23 Pool, `pool.query(text, values)`: unnamed statements (Parse every time), text results, default type parsers.
drivers.pg-named: node-postgres 8.23 Pool with named prepared statements (`{ name, text, values }`, one name per distinct SQL text): its fastest documented mode for repeated queries.
drivers.pg-native: node-postgres 8.23 `pg.native` Pool over libpq (pg-native 3.9, libpq 18 client), unnamed statements.
drivers.pg-native-named: pg.native Pool with named prepared statements.
drivers.postgres.js: postgres.js 3.4.9 defaults: `prepare: true` (named statements), `sql.unsafe(text, params)`, implicit pipelining on each connection, `fetch_types: true`.
drivers.postgres.js-noprep: postgres.js 3.4.9 with `prepare: false` (unnamed statements, for transaction poolers without prepared-statement support).
drivers.bun.sql: Bun.sql (built-in Zig client) defaults: `prepare: true`, `sql.unsafe(text, params)`, pipelining.
drivers.neon: @neondatabase/serverless 1.2 Pool (bundled pg over WebSocket) through Neon's Go wsproxy on localhost; unnamed statements; `coalesceWrites: false` (the default batches writes with setTimeout(0), ≥1 ms per round trip on Node); `pipelineConnect: false` (needs cleartext password auth).
drivers.deno-postgres: deno-postgres (jsr:@db/postgres 0.19.5) Pool, lazy connections, `queryObject(text, args)`, as shipped: it writes Parse/Bind/Describe/Execute/Sync as separate socket writes without TCP_NODELAY, so each query waits for a delayed ACK (~40 ms on Linux).
drivers.deno-postgres-nodelay: deno-postgres with `Deno.connect` patched to call `setNoDelay(true)` on every socket: its best case (not configurable through its API).
